status: proposed generation methods for evaluator-first development; no production policy or model selected

population.selection: Eight conditional cards selected from the universal-scope methods; canonical self-labels are not approval.

cards.title: Write little, judge the rest
cards.claim: Use bounded selection from authored, checked responses when the response space is finite and the choice can be judged against supplied evidence.
applies_when: A finite set of response or feedback moves can cover the specified task.
The choice judge has the evidence and a demonstrated abstention path.
actions: Separate text that truly requires generation from selection, marking and routing.
Prepare response alternatives before the learner attempt where this design fits.
checks: Trace every learner-visible line to an authored or verified source.
Test correct, wrong, partial and uncertain answers against the chooser before asserting coverage.
cards.refusal_or_fallback: If no alternative fits or the judge is unsure, withhold the chosen reply or use a previously verified fallback; do not invent a confident diagnosis.
limits: The recorded latency comparison is from one Grade 9 paragraph-coach route, not a universal speed or learning result.
A live response tailored to the learner's wording may be stronger in some tasks; this card does not ban it.

evidence.quote: It is now a Jev choice among four authored steps, filled with the student's own words,

cards.title: Verified facts as the factual source
cards.claim: Supply a pinned, verified fact and source packet for factual questions; treat it as the claim boundary and independently check the generated item's claims against it.
applies_when: The item asserts checkable facts about a source, event, text or curriculum target.
The authoritative fact or source can be identified and supplied.
actions: Select source facts at the exact target scope before drafting.
Keep source text, derived claims and model-written wording distinguishable.
checks: For every material claim, record the supporting source span and test whether the source actually entails it.
Challenge unsupported facts introduced after retrieval; verify the key and every distractor separately.
cards.refusal_or_fallback: If a required fact or source cannot be verified, hold the item or use a separately verified source; do not fill the gap with plausible model research.
limits: The source report's 25% to 100% comparison used five samples per condition and is not a general effect estimate.
Retrieval and a grounding prompt do not ensure the writer follows the source; post-retrieval claim construction failed in a separate AP analysis.
The canonical record is contested, so this is a conditional source-control method, not a universal RAG endorsement.

evidence.quote: Flash research stage hallucinated facts that poisoned the compile step. MongoDB verified facts are better.
Ran data-driven benchmarks (5 samples each) to decide what to optimize
evidence.origin: source-declared sample-size limit for the comparison

evidence.quote: Pipeline grounding (retrieval, primary sources) doesn't fix this because the failure happens AFTER retrieval
evidence.origin: first-party counterevidence; content failure after retrieval

cards.title: Examples teach form, not facts
cards.claim: Use vetted examples to communicate output form while keeping their incidental factual content out of a new item's evidence base.
applies_when: Examples are supplied to a model to demonstrate an item or response format.
The examples' facts are not independently relevant to the requested target.
actions: Choose examples for structure and remove or replace unrelated facts where possible.
Keep target facts in a separately pinned source packet.
checks: Inspect output for copied dates, names, source attributions, answers and topic-specific details from demonstrations.
Compare the example-bearing request with a no-example or structure-only control on fresh targets.
cards.refusal_or_fallback: If the item imports an example's unsupported content, discard or revise it and re-evaluate; do not treat fluent format as factual validity.
limits: One recorded prompt sweep found contamination and a lower pass rate, but did not prove that all examples hurt.
Same-topic demonstrations may be appropriate when their content is also part of the verified source packet; no fixed example count is selected.

evidence.quote: The few-shot examples gave the model specific historical content (dates, sources, attributions from the examples) that contaminated its generation.

cards.title: Refuse rather than ship a weak item
cards.claim: Make an unsatisfied source, format or quality gate visible; a fallback is eligible only when its own item and provenance have been verified for this request.
applies_when: A required source or response-format input is missing, or this item type has not been evaluated for the requested route.
A fallback would otherwise create filler, fabricated sources or an untested item.
actions: Return a typed refusal or hold with the missing requirement.
Consider a stored, separately verified item only if its target, source, version and validity conditions still match.
checks: Verify a fallback's source and answerability independently of the failed candidate.
Record failure, verified fallback and fresh generation as different provenance states.
cards.refusal_or_fallback: If neither a valid candidate nor a request-matched vetted fallback exists, emit no item.
limits: The source's DBQ rule concerns real-source documents in that route, not every question type.
The canonical record is contested: later validation allowed a marked cached fallback, so blanket rejection of all fallbacks is unsupported.
No retry count or production release threshold is selected here.

evidence.quote: Without D13: do not generate this DBQ. Return an error indicating "real-source documents required".
The generic DBQ fallback padded missing source documents with curriculum facts using `Retrieved APUSH Unit {unit} source N`, which produced fake repetitive documents.
evidence.origin: observed fallback failure in mixed-version partial run

cards.title: Measure a generator on one try
cards.claim: Report raw first-attempt item quality separately from a bank's filtered or repaired served quality.
applies_when: Comparing generators, versions, item types or prompt changes.
A route can retry, repair, rerank, cache, filter or substitute candidates.
actions: Freeze input set, source packet, model/version, decoding and evaluator before the measured run.
Record the first response and every subsequent repair, selection or substitution as separate states.
checks: Report denominators and pass/abstain/failure counts by item type and source scope.
Keep raw one-attempt, best-of-many and served-bank results in separate columns; disclose evaluator version and calibration limits.
cards.refusal_or_fallback: When first-attempt data or frozen versions are missing, label the comparison unmeasured rather than inferring a raw pass rate from served items.
limits: The cited AP handoff defined a raw-K1 protocol but explicitly had not run the planned InceptBench test.
A separate one-shot baseline used its own grader and version; its percentages cannot be compared directly with later evaluator versions.
No sample quota or success threshold from that AP handoff is adopted here.

evidence.quote: one candidate, one attempt, no retry, reranking, repair, cache substitution, rejection sampling, best-of-N, or
evidence.origin: frozen AP evaluation design, not a completed run

evidence.quote: No InceptBench run has been executed for this APUSH handoff.

cards.title: Provenance for every factual field
cards.claim: Track factual authority at field level when a source record mixes official text, human interpretation and generated additions.
applies_when: A single curriculum, source or item record contains fields from different authors or generation processes.
actions: Label each factual field with its origin, revision and verification status.
Mark model-inferred or missing-source fields as hypotheses, not official facts.
checks: Audit whether any generated misconception, boundary, attribution or key is being promoted by a record-level source label.
Check that downstream prompts and datasets preserve the field labels.
cards.refusal_or_fallback: If the required field's authority cannot be established, withhold its factual use or route it for source review.
limits: A generated field is not automatically false; it may become usable after independent verification.
The source audit concerns one AP curriculum corpus, not a measured cross-domain error rate.

evidence.quote: Different fields in the same record can have different provenance.

cards.title: Write the sequence before the items
cards.claim: Use the course's declared progression and exposure sequence as input to item design so available questions do not silently determine what is taught.
applies_when: Generating an ordered set for a course or lesson whose progression, prerequisites or taught content matter.
actions: Ask for the progression policy, entry assumptions, target knowledge and planned teaching order.
Tag each candidate item's role and placement against that supplied plan.
checks: Check that an item does not assess untaught material unless it is explicitly diagnostic or transfer.
Review repeated evidence and revealed answers across the ordered sequence.
cards.refusal_or_fallback: If the necessary sequence is unavailable, label the output as unplaced candidate questions and withhold claims of course fit.
limits: The TI source is internal curriculum guidance, not evidence that one progression strategy works everywhere.
This card does not choose the course's content, grade, prerequisite strictness or sequence policy.

evidence.quote: You cannot outsource sequence judgement to the model; you must supply the policy.
evidence.origin: internal curriculum guidance, not measured learner outcome

cards.title: Keep the writer and judge apart
cards.claim: Keep private evaluator scores, identities, raw returns and holdout labels outside the generator's inputs; screen student-facing text for attempts to steer the judge.
applies_when: An evaluator's decisions can be fed back into generation or repair.
The generator writes text later seen by a model-based judge.
actions: Expose only the public authoring contract to the writer.
If development feedback is allowed, translate it into ordinary editorial issues without private labels or raw judge output; keep final holdout feedback sealed.
checks: Inspect prompts, logs and artifacts for evaluator score labels, metric weights, raw judge JSON or holdout answers crossing the boundary.
Void or quarantine candidate text that addresses the judge instead of the learner.
cards.refusal_or_fallback: If the boundary or provenance cannot be established, do not use that run as independent evaluator evidence.
limits: The cited source is one repair pipeline's contract; it does not prove that its note-cleaning implementation is correct.
No comparative study showed sanitized notes improve generation; final qualification still needs untouched holdouts and independent labels.

evidence.quote: The generator must never see evaluator names, scores, metric labels, or raw
